extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, USPTO officials, policymakers, and patent litigators
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules (deadlines, burdens, joinder, estoppel, remedies, USPTO rulemaking duties, and related administrative provisions) implementing post-grant review, inter partes review, supplemental examination, covered business-method proceedings, and other patent-practice changes in the America Invents Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12-month filing deadline for inter partes review
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review must be sought by a party within 12 months of the date when the party is served with a complaint for infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates a time limit tying a defendant’s ability to file an inter partes review petition to the date of service of an infringement complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prompt infringement suit on stay for preliminary injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent owner sues for infringement within 3 months of the patent’s issue, a pending petition for post-grant review or the institution of such a proceeding may not serve as a basis for staying the court’s consideration of the patent owner’s motion for a preliminary injunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recently filed infringement suit (within 3 months of patent issue) prevents the mere existence or institution of a post-grant review petition from staying the court's preliminary injunction considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may allow joinder of petitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may allow other petitioners to join an inter partes or post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joinder of additional petitioners into an instituted review is within the Director’s discretion under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may consolidate proceedings and decline repetitive matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may consolidate multiple proceedings or matters concerning the same patent and decline requests for repeated proceedings on the same question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation and refusals to permit repeated attacks on the same question are tools to promote efficiency and avoid duplicative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel following inter partes and post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes and post-grant petitioners are estopped from raising in a subsequent Office proceeding any issue that they raised or reasonably could have raised in the inter partes or post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes petitioners are also estopped from raising in civil litigation or an ITC proceeding any issue that they raised or could have raised in the inter partes review. Post-grant petitioners are only estopped in civil litigation or ITC proceedings for issues they actually raised in the post-grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on post-grant review of reissue patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant review may not be used to challenge claims in a reissue patent that are the same as or narrower than claims in the original patent if the time for seeking review of the original patent has lapsed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents re-litigating or re-challenging claim scope via post-grant review when original-review windows have closed and claims are not broader than originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director rulemaking: public file requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations that make the file in proceedings public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations must ensure public access to proceeding files, subject to protective orders for confidential material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director rulemaking: standards for instituting reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations that define standards for instituting reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations must set the substantive and threshold tests (e.g., reasonable likelihood of prevailing) for initiating inter partes and post-grant reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director rulemaking: allow submission of additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations that allow submission of additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should permit relevant additional evidence or information to be filed in prescribed ways and within prescribed windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director rulemaking: define relationship to other proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations that establish and govern review and its relationship to other proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations must clarify how post-grant/inter partes reviews interact with district court litigation, ITC proceedings, reexamination, and other USPTO processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director rulemaking: time limit for requesting joinder in inter partes review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations that set a time limit for requesting joinder in inter partes review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations will define when and how potential joinder requests must be made to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director rulemaking: standards for discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations that set standards for discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations will limit and define the scope of permissible discovery in review proceedings to balance party needs and expedition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director rulemaking: sanctions for abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations that prescribe sanctions for abuse of the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations must provide remedies or penalties where petitioners or other parties misuse review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director rulemaking: protective orders for confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations that provide for protective orders for confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should allow confidential business information to be protected while enabling meaningful review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of patent owner to file a response after institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations that allow the patent owner to file a response after an inter partes review has been instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even after institution, patent owner must have an opportunity to respond under rules set by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner amendment rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may submit one amendment with a reasonable number of substitute claims, and additional amendments either as agreed to by the parties for settlement, for good cause shown in post-grant review, or as prescribed in regulations by the Director in inter partes review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a right to amend claims but limits scope and further amendments subject to agreement, good cause, or regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations that provide either party with the right to an oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either party in an instituted review will have an opportunity for an oral hearing as regulated by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year statutory time limit (with 6-month extension) for completion of proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations that set a 1-year time limit for completion of the proceeding, with a 6-month extension for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution-to-final-decision target is 1 year, extendable by 6 months for good cause to promote timely resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for petitioner to file written comments after institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations that provide the petitioner with at least one opportunity to file written comments after the proceeding is instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners retain an opportunity to submit written commentary post-institution under the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director must consider integrity and efficiency when prescribing regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: In prescribing regulations, the Director shall consider the integrity of the patent system and the efficient operation of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking discretion must balance systemic integrity (quality of patents) and USPTO operational efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Trial and Appeal Board shall conduct review proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Trial and Appeal Board shall conduct review proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB (replacing Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences) is the tribunal charged with post-grant, inter partes and related review functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenger burden of proof: preponderance of the evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The challenger shall have the burden of proving unpatentability by a preponderance of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard of proof in these USPTO-administered reviews is preponderance, not clear-and-convincing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement effect on estoppel
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may agree to settle review proceedings, in which case estoppel shall not apply and a copy of the settlement agreement shall be filed in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement can avoid statutory estoppel consequences but must be filed in the Office for record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final written decision and certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Trial and Appeal Board shall issue a final written decision and a certificate cancelling, confirming, or incorporating claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB final decisions result in an official certificate that changes the patent claim set accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal route from final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with a final written decision may appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal Circuit is the appellate path for review of PTAB final written decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for Director regulations and transition provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall issue regulations implementing the new reviews within 1 year, and create transition provisions for proceedings pending between the enactment of the Act and the full implementation of the new reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking and transitional rules are time-limited obligations to ensure implementation within one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written statements of patent owner as citable prior art (Sec. 301 amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sec. 301 is amended to include written statements of the patent owner filed in proceedings before a Federal court or the Office as citable prior art; the section provides rules for submitting such statements and the limitations on their use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent-owner statements filed in certain proceedings may be used as prior art with specified submission rules and usage limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director-initiated reexamination based on third-party citations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may determine whether to initiate reexamination on the Director’s own initiative based on citations by any person other than the owner of the patent under section 301 or 302.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO can open reexamination/ex parte review sua sponte in response to third-party-cited references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party preissuance submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a mechanism for third parties to submit timely pre-issuance information relevant to the examination of the application, including a concise statement of the relevance of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties can submit prior art and concise relevance statements during prosecution under prescribed timing and format rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of venue to Eastern District of Virginia
rubrics_metrics.description: The venue for certain district court challenges of USPTO decisions is changed from the District of Columbia to the Eastern District of Virginia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Litigation challenging USPTO decisions will (in certain cases) be filed in EDVA, where the USPTO resides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director fee-setting authority and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has rulemaking authority to set or adjust any fee under specified sections, provided fee amounts reasonably compensate the USPTO; the Director shall consult advisory committees; any proposed fee change (including rationale) must be published in the Federal Register with not less than 45 days public comment; the Director shall notify Congress of any final proposed fee change and Congress shall have up to 45 days to consider and comment before the change becomes effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee changes must follow consultation, notice-and-comment, and congressional notification periods to ensure transparency and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference patent fee schedule inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act includes the current patent fee schedule in the text as a reference point for any future adjustments by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutory schedule establishes a baseline for future fee rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination threshold and timing (Sec. 257)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Sec. 257, the Director must initially determine whether a petitioner’s request for supplemental examination of one or more items in the request raises a new question of patentability, and must make this determination within 3 months of receiving a request for supplemental examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 3-month statutory clock governs the Director’s threshold determination on supplemental examination requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination outcome: reexamination if threshold met
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director issues a certificate affirming that the threshold is met, a reexamination shall be ordered and will be conducted according to the procedures under Chapter 30 (ex parte reexamination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A positive threshold finding triggers an ex parte reexamination under existing Chapter 30 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of supplemental examination on inequitable conduct defenses
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent cannot be held unenforceable on the basis of conduct relating to information that had not been considered, was inadequately considered, or was incorrect in a prior examination if the information was considered, reconsidered, or corrected during the supplemental examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information addressed in supplemental examination cannot be used to render the patent unenforceable for inequitable conduct, although challengers may still argue the Office’s conclusion was erroneous; three exceptions apply (certain drug application allegations, actions before ITC or court unless supplemental exam concluded beforehand, and fraud on the USPTO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director is authorized to establish fees, by regulation, to help defray the cost of a supplemental examination, in addition to those charged pursuant to Chapter 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental examination may carry separate regulatory fees set by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: No limitation on criminal or antitrust laws or Director’s investigatory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in Section 12 limits the application of criminal or antitrust laws or the ability of the USPTO Director to investigate and sanction persons or their representatives for misconduct before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental examination protections do not shield misconduct from criminal, antitrust, or USPTO investigatory/sanction authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royalties retention for nonprofit GOCO facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprofit organization that has a funding agreement for the operation of a Government-owned-contractor-operated facility may retain 85% of licensing royalties in excess of the amount equal to 5% of the annual budget of the facility (amendment to Sec. 202(c)(7)(E)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusts financial retention rules for certain nonprofit-operated government facilities to encourage licensing participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax strategies deemed insufficient to distinguish over prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies for reducing, avoiding, or deferring tax liability shall be deemed insufficient to differentiate an invention from the prior art; the provision is directed to tax strategies (a subset of business methods) and is not intended to deny patent protection for inventions that consist of tax preparation software or tools used solely to enter data; separable non-tax aspects of an invention remain enforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that encompass tax strategies cannot rely on the novelty/non-obviousness of the tax strategy to overcome sections 102/103; software novel as software is not necessarily affected unless the claim itself is a tax strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO consultation with Treasury/IRS on tax strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may seek advice and assistance from Treasury and the IRS to better recognize tax strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interagency consultation is authorized to help identify tax-strategy prior art and ensure such matters remain in the public domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of best mode as basis for invalidity or unenforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 15 amends Sec. 282(b) by removing the failure to disclose the best mode under section 112 as a basis for canceling or holding either invalid or unenforceable a patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best-mode nondisclosure no longer provides a basis to invalidate or render claims unenforceable, though best mode may still be required to be disclosed in application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual marking allowed and USPTO report on effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsection (a) allows a patent holder to satisfy Sec. 287 marking requirements by affixing to a patented article the word 'patent' or 'pat.' together with an Internet address that the public can access free of charge to determine the status of the patent; USPTO to report to Congress on effectiveness within 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Virtual marking via a public URL is an accepted alternative to marking with numbers; USPTO will study its effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: False marking reforms: qui tam and damages rules and safe harbors
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the United States may sue for the qui tam penalty; a person who has suffered a competitive injury may bring a civil action in US district court for compensatory damages; persons liable under Sec. 292 are protected during a 3-year window beginning on the date the patent at issue expires; beyond the 3-year window, protection applies if marking is consistent with virtual marking provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrows qui tam enforcement, preserves injured-party damages claims, and provides limited temporal safe harbors to reduce abusive false-marking litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice-of-counsel evidence not probative of willfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure of an infringer to obtain the advice of counsel regarding any allegedly infringed patent, or the failure to present such advice to the court or jury, may not be used to prove that the accused infringer willfully infringed the patent or intended to induce infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrew the evidentiary weight of advice-of-counsel or lack thereof in willfulness/inducement determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional program for covered business-method (CBM) patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates a transitional program to allow post-grant review of the validity of covered business method patents, modeled after post-grant review but limited: a petition cannot be accepted unless the petitioner or his real party in interest has been sued for or charged with infringement; estoppel bars later asserting invalidity before the ITC or Federal court on a ground considered and resulting in a written decision by the agency; program takes effect 1 year after enactment and sunsets after 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM program is targeted, retroactive coverage applies to patents before/on/after effective date (with statutory exceptions), and provides estoppel protections from re-assertion of grounds decided by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: District court stay criteria for CBM-related infringement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: A US district court shall decide to grant a stay based on: (A) whether a stay will simplify issues and streamline the trial; (B) whether discovery is complete and whether a trial date has been set; (C) whether a stay would unduly prejudice the non-moving party or present a clear tactical advantage for the moving party; and (D) whether a stay will reduce the burden of litigation on the parties and on the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts must weigh judicial efficiency, litigation progress, prejudice/tactical considerations, and overall burden reduction when deciding CBM-related stays; interlocutory appeal permitted and Federal Circuit review may be de novo.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBM definition (financial/business-method focus, excludes technological inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'covered business method patent' as one that claims a method or corresponding apparatus for performing data processing or other operations used in the practice, administration, or management of a financial product or service, except that it does not include patents for technological inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrows CBM scope to financial-service related inventions and excludes technological inventions to avoid overbroad application.

rubrics_metrics.name: No change to Sec. 101 subject-matter categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in Section 18 shall be construed as amending or interpreting categories of patent-eligible subject matter under Sec. 101 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM provisions are not intended to alter judicial or statutory interpretations of patentable subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holmes Group abrogation and state-court jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsections (a) through (d) enact the so-called Holmes Group fix, abrogating Holmes Group, Inc. v. Vornado and more fully precluding state court jurisdiction over patent legal claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies federal exclusive jurisdiction over patent claims to avoid parallel state-court litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder limits for accused infringers (Sec. 299)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accused infringers may be joined in one action as defendants or counterclaim defendants only if: (1) any right to relief is asserted against the parties jointly, severally, or in the alternative with respect to or arising out of the same transaction, occurrence, or series of transactions or occurrences relating to the making, using, importing, offering for sale, or selling of the same accused product or process; and (2) questions of fact common to all defendants or counterclaim defendants will arise in the action. Accused infringers may not be joined based solely on allegations that they each have infringed the patent or patents in suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits multi-defendant joinder to cases with transactional and factual commonality to prevent fishing expeditions combining unrelated defendants.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO travel expense and administrative judge pay authority
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO may expend funds to cover subsistence and travel-related expenses of non-Federal employees attending intellectual property programs hosted by the agency; the Director may fix the rate of basic pay for administrative patent and trademark judges at a rate not greater than that payable for level III of the Executive Pay Schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes administrative funding and pay-setting to support agency programs and attract adjudicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Public Enterprise Fund financial administration and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes the 'United States Patent and Trademark Office Public Enterprise Fund' replacing the appropriation account; Director authorized to collect all user fee revenue, create a revolving fund available until expended; Director must submit annual reports to Congress summarizing operations, operating plan, modernization plans and progress, and audit results; requires annual independent audit and submission of a 'business-type' budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates revolving-fund financial structure with reporting, audit, and budget obligations to increase fiscal transparency and flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satellite office establishment and selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Director shall establish three or more satellite offices in the United States subject to available resources within 3 years; purposes include increasing outreach, enhancing examiner retention, and improving quality of patent examination; required considerations in selecting locations include geographic diversity and reliance upon previous evaluations; Director must report to Congress within three fiscal years on rationale, progress, and whether purposes are being achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates satellite office creation with explicit selection criteria and reporting to assess effectiveness in reaching statutory goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Ombudsman Program for small businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Director shall establish and maintain in the USPTO a Patent Ombudsman Program, whose staff shall provide support and services relating to patent filings to small business concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides dedicated assistance and support to small-business filers to improve access to the patent system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority examination for technologies important to competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Amends Sec. 2(b)(2) to permit the USPTO to prioritize the examination of applications for products, processes, or technologies that are important to the national economy or national competitiveness without recovering the aggregate extra cost of providing such prioritization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows USPTO to expedite examination for critical technologies as a policy tool to support national competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting rules for 60-day period for patent term extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies USPTO counting rules: if the application is transmitted after 4:30 pm, EST, on a business day, or is transmitted on a day that is not a business day, the product addressed shall be deemed to receive 'permission' on the next business day; defines 'business day' as Mon–Fri excluding legal holidays under 5 U.S.C. §6103; applies to certain pending or future extension applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies time-stamping and business-day rules to determine timely filing for patent-term-extension calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study on implementation and reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Director required to conduct a study on the manner in which the Act is being implemented by the USPTO, review patent policies and practices of the Federal Government with respect to patent rights and related issues, and submit results with recommendations to the Senate and House Judiciary Committees not later than 4 years after enactment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates an evaluative study and congressional report to assess implementation and suggest further changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro bono program to assist under-resourced inventors and small businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Director required to work with and support intellectual law associations across the country to establish pro bono programs to assist financially under-resourced independent inventors and small businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages coordinated pro bono assistance to expand access to patent representation for those with limited resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided, the Act takes effect 12 months after the date of enactment and applies to any patent issued on or after that effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the general one-year delayed effective date and specifies patent-issuance applicability; certain provisions may have different effective dates as noted.
